title.en: List the advantages of modular programming

say.en: A tailor stitching 40 uniforms does not reinvent the shirt pattern each time. He cuts one pattern and reuses it. Functions are the patterns of programming. In this lesson: Explain what a function is.
List the advantages of modular programming.

body.en: A *function* is a named group of statements that does one specific task. It runs only when it is called. A long program can be divided into many such functions; this is called modular programming.
body.kn: ಫಂಕ್ಷನ್ ಎಂದರೆ ಒಂದು ನಿರ್ದಿಷ್ಟ ಕೆಲಸ ಮಾಡುವ, ಹೆಸರಿರುವ ಹೇಳಿಕೆಗಳ ಗುಂಪು. ಅದನ್ನು ಕರೆದಾಗ ಮಾತ್ರ ಅದು ಕಾರ್ಯನಿರ್ವಹಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ದೊಡ್ಡ ಪ್ರೋಗ್ರಾಮನ್ನು ಹಲವು ಫಂಕ್ಷನ್‌ಗಳಾಗಿ ವಿಭಜಿಸುವುದನ್ನು ಮಾಡ್ಯುಲರ್ ಪ್ರೋಗ್ರಾಮಿಂಗ್ ಎನ್ನುತ್ತಾರೆ.

say.en: Each function does one well-defined task.

title.en: On the board: Why we divide a program into functions

say.en: Without functions, the same lines are copied wherever they are needed.
A copied mistake must be corrected in every copy, and the program grows long and hard to read.
With functions, we write each task once, give it a name, and call it wherever it is needed.
This is modular programming: the program is built from small named modules.
Functions make the program readable, shorter, easier to test, and let a team share the work.

body.en: *Functions* increase readability because each part has a clear name. They reduce code length because the same code is reused. They make testing and correcting errors easier, and different team members can write different functions.
body.kn: ಫಂಕ್ಷನ್‌ಗಳು ಪ್ರೋಗ್ರಾಮನ್ನು ಓದಲು ಸುಲಭ ಮಾಡುತ್ತವೆ, ಕೋಡ್ ಮರುಬಳಕೆಯಿಂದ ಉದ್ದ ಕಡಿಮೆಯಾಗುತ್ತದೆ, ದೋಷ ಹುಡುಕಿ ಸರಿಪಡಿಸುವುದು ಸುಲಭ, ಮತ್ತು ತಂಡದಲ್ಲಿ ಕೆಲಸ ಹಂಚಿಕೊಳ್ಳಬಹುದು.

tagline.en: Output questions with default and global variables, possible outputs with the random module, and short functions to write on lists and strings.

myth.en: random.randint(1, 5) behaves like range(1, 5), so it never gives 5.

truth.en: randint(a, b) includes both ends, so 5 is possible. It is randrange(1, 5) that stops at 4. Learners carry the "stop is excluded" rule from range() and slicing to every function. randint is the exception.

say.en: Track parameter values separately from the caller's variables in every call.
A list passed to a function and changed in place stays changed.
randint(a, b) includes both ends; randrange(a, b) excludes b.
For possible outputs, find each random variable's range first.
Return results from functions unless asked to display them.

goal.en: Output questions with default and global variables, possible outputs with the random module, and short functions to write on lists and strings.

question.en: k = random.randint(2, 4); print("AB" * k). Which output is not possible?

explain.en: k is 2, 3 or 4, so "AB" repeats 2 to 4 times. A single AB would need k = 1.

task.en: Match each call to its output.

explain.en: Hampi Utsav has a, i, U, a. Malayalam reads the same backwards once lowered. Slicing from index 2 and adding the first two items shifts left by 2.

takeaway.en: Track parameter values separately from the caller's variables in every call.

narration.en: Many people think: random.randint(1, 5) behaves like range(1, 5), so it never gives 5. Actually: randint(a, b) includes both ends, so 5 is possible. It is randrange(1, 5) that stops at 4. Learners carry the "stop is excluded" rule from range() and slicing to every function. randint is the exception.
